params.body:
## Why

Admitting a source was a command on the server (`bin/source-state.mjs admit`) and nothing in the Observatory. The desk read, the guide and the morning mail all point people to the Sources page to admit, where no such act existed. On 19 November 2026 production held 22 trials that had passed and stayed on trial, and with the trial waves capped at 150 running trials, trials that never close stop new ones from starting.

The slow part of admitting is finding the source's terms of use. The Standard admits only on terms that allow a paid product and says a person reads them before admission.

## What

**A person decides, in the tool.** `POST /sources/:id/terms {terms}` for editors and admins. The person says what the terms are; the trial is decided by that:

- `allowed` or `attribution` (the Standard's `admit.allowTerms`): the same `admit` move as the command, with the scorecard verdict, so a trial that has not passed is still refused.
- `non-commercial` or `forbidden`: the trial is rejected, the terms are kept on the row, and the note says why.
- `unknown`, a missing name, or the engine as the one deciding: refused.

**The engine looks the terms up and stops there.** `packages/core/source-terms.mjs`:

- finds the site a source belongs to (the listing's site, else the feed's host), reads the home page and takes the links that look like terms (terms, voorwaarden, conditions générales, Nutzungsbedingungen, copyright, legal), same site only, at most two;
- a model reads those pages and names one of the Standard's values, with the sentence it rests on and one sentence why;
- the suggestion is kept only when that sentence is on the page as quoted (case and spacing aside). Otherwise the finding is `unknown` with the reason;
- the result goes in a new `terms_found` column. `terms` and `state` are never written by the engine.

Pages are fetched with the existing `fetchPage` (public addresses only), and the prompt names the page text as material, not instructions. A page that tells the model what to answer can at most produce a suggestion a person still reads.

It runs at the end of the scout run, five sources a run, for trials whose verdict is `needs-terms`, and not again for a source within 30 days.

**For the Sources page:** `GET /sources/trials` gives every trial with its verdict, its figures and what was found.

**Wording made true.** The desk read now tells apart trials whose terms were found (wait for a person) and trials still to be looked up (the Observatory does that itself). The guide says where admitting happens and that it is not done through Ask.

## Checked

- `test/source-terms.test.mjs`, 13 cases: finding the site and the links; a suggestion stands only on a sentence that is on the page; a wrong value, a short or invented sentence and unreadable output all give `unknown`; the engine writes neither `terms` nor `state`, looks up only trials that passed, a few a run, and not twice; a person admits a passed trial, turns one down on terms that do not allow, and cannot admit a trial that has not passed, nor can the engine.
- Full suite 1797/1797, `tsc` clean.
- Not tried against a live site or a live model: how often a usable sentence is found is not known yet.

## After merge

No step on the box: the columns are added on first use. The dashboard change that shows the block on the Sources page follows in its own pull request and needs this one deployed first.
params.title: Admitting a source moves into the tool, with its terms looked up
